SiMR Basis Geometry Ablations: Role of w, Orthogonal Varimax Subspace Rotation (pysimlr v0.2.17), Quantile Sparseness (default=0.5), and ADNI-MCI Anatomical Attribution

This standalone report summarizes the reproducible ablation experiments evaluating (1) the approximate Stiefel retraction weight w = 0.5 in nsa_flow, (2) why unrotated PCA initialization without Varimax rotation or row-mean removal leaves Component 1 (v1) dense, (3) how default Orthogonal Varimax Subspace Rotation (varimax=True in pysimlr v0.2.17 and nsa_flow) redistributes the global mean mode across all k axes to boost unthresholded (q = None) sparsity from 15% to 66.1% (`[24, 12, 26]` active DKT regions) out-of-the-box, (4) how the R ANTsR::simlr-style quantile sparseness parameter (default=0.5, with 0.85 isolating 9-region Braak neurofibrillary panels) enforces explicit cardinality bounds, and (5) the regenerated manuscript Figures 3.5 and 3.8.

varimax = True
Default in pysimlr v0.2.17: raises unthresholded ADNI-MCI sparsity from 15.0% to 66.1% (`[24, 12, 26]` active parcels) and balances Heart/Diabetes V-matrices
w = 0.50
Default NSA-Flow sweet spot: EffRank = 3.00, D = 0.0006, 64.8% sparsity in 4.0s (vs. EffRank = 2.02 collapse at w = 0.01)
q ∈ {0.5, 0.85}
Universal default sparseness = 0.50 (discovery) and focal biomarker panel 0.85 (CogPC1 R2 = 0.1923, 88.0% sparse, 9/62 active DKT regions)
1 − 1/k Law
Non-negative (V ≥ 0) disjoint support bound: 50.0% (k=2), 66.7% (k=3), 80.0% (k=5), 87.5% (k=8), 91.7% (k=12)

3. Resolving the "Component 1 = Mean" Effect: Varimax Rotation, Row-Mean Control & Rank k Sparsity

Under unrotated column-centered PCA initialization (varimax=False, q=None), Component 1 (v1) absorbs the global cortical thickness floor (only 3.2%–14.5% sparse). In pysimlr v0.2.17, default Orthogonal Varimax Subspace Rotation (varimax=True) rotates the k-dimensional subspace prior to non-negative retraction, achieving 66.1% unthresholded sparsity directly on standard column-centered features without requiring manual subject row-mean centering.

4. Quantile-Based sparseness Parameter Ablation (default=0.5, Operating Points 0.5 & 0.8 in pysimlr)

Combining nsa_flow(varimax=True) with quantile sparseness (default=0.5 everywhere in pysimlr, with 0.5 and 0.8/0.85 as canonical operating points) enforces explicit cardinality bounds per column. At sparseness = 0.85, non-negative SiMR achieves CogPC1 R2 = 0.1923 (exceeding dense PCA 0.1904) with exactly (9, 9, 9)/62 active DKT cortical regions per component.

5. Regenerated Figure 3.5: ADNI-MCI 62-Region Cortical Thickness Localization & Axis-Alignment Negative Controls

Panel A2 illustrates the unrotated PCA+NSA failure mode (q = None, 15% sparse, where v1 absorbs 53/62 regions), Panel A3 demonstrates out-of-the-box pysimlr v0.2.17 Default Varimax+NSA (q = None, 66% sparse, `[24, 12, 26]` active parcels), and Panel A4 & B show Focal SiMR (q = 0.85, 88% sparse, R2 = 0.192) isolating Braak Stages IV–V, Braak Stages I–III, and the Frontocingulate Salience Network while sparing primary sensorimotor cortex. Furthermore, 3-seed algorithmic negative controls (adni_mci_axis_alignment_controls.csv) confirm that rotating the learned scores by in-fold PCA (PCA-Rotated Score Control) leaves linear R2 identically unchanged (`Flow-SiMR-V` 0.2403 → 0.2403; `LEND` 0.2418 → 0.2418; `SiMLR-LBFGSB` 0.1650 → 0.1650) while degrading single-axis Random Forest R2 (`SiMLR-LBFGSB` 0.1123 → 0.0879; non-negative `LEND` 0.1617 → 0.1416), and permuting basis rows within each view (Support-Shuffled Basis Control) collapses Random Forest R2 by 60%–65% (`Flow-SiMR-V` 0.1798 → 0.0627; `LEND` 0.1725 → 0.0690; `NEDPP` 0.1563 → 0.0668).

6. Regenerated Figure 3.8: Hierarchical Sparse Basis Localization on Heart & Diabetes (Varimax + NSA-Flow)

With varimax=True + nsa_flow support projection (q = 0.50), every view of the Heart Disease and Diabetes cohorts partitions cleanly into balanced, non-overlapping physiological subnetworks (eliminating the pre-v0.2.17 pathology where L1 absorbed 80%–86% of features and L2 collapsed to a single-feature residual):
